name: Disappointment Peak
generated_description:
At 9,744 feet, Disappointment Peak is a summit in Washington. The Disappointment Peak Trail covers 1.2 miles with about 1,896 feet of elevation gain — a steep, sustained climb.

The Route

The climbing is spread fairly evenly from start to finish rather than stacked into one steep section. The steepest stretch arrives around mile 0, gaining roughly 2,900 feet per mile — expect a slow, deliberate pace through here. From the trailhead at about 4,190 feet, the route tops out near 6,086 feet.

Getting There

The trailhead is at 48.11524, -121.17475 (tap for driving directions). It's roughly 65 miles northeast of Seattle, Washington. Arrive early on weekends — trailhead lots at popular peaks fill quickly, and cell service is often unreliable once you leave the highway.

When to Go

Late May through October is the main season. Snow and ice linger into spring and return early in fall at this latitude and elevation; in winter this becomes a different, more serious undertaking requiring traction devices and warm layers.

Know Before You Go

Most hikers should budget about 1.5 hours of moving time; add margin for breaks, photos and the descent. Download the GPX track from this page before you go — cell coverage is unreliable in the mountains and a saved route works offline in any GPS app. Conditions change: verify current access, closures and weather with the official land manager before you go. Trail data is sourced from OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL).

Looking to link objectives or plan a weekend? Nearby summits include Seven Fingered Jack, Bonanza Peak and Mount Fernow — each has its own guide on this site.
